subject: maths
promptStrong: Give me a challenging GCSE exam-style question on {lo}, then mark my answer.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for GCSE Maths simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake.

questions.q: Find the median of 4, 8, 6, 2, 9.
questions.explain: Order the data: 2, 4, 6, 8, 9. The middle value is 6.

questions.q: Find the range of 12, 7, 15, 9, 20.
questions.explain: Range = largest - smallest = 20 - 7 = 13.

questions.q: The mean of five numbers is 10. Four of them are 8, 12, 9 and 15. Find the fifth.
questions.explain: Total must be 5×10 = 50. The four given sum to 44, so the fifth is 50 - 44 = 6.

questions.q: A survey records scores: score 1 (freq 4), 2 (freq 6), 3 (freq 10). Find the mean.
For a frequency table, the mean is found by which calculation?
questions.explain: The mean from a frequency table is the sum of (frequency × value) divided by the total frequency: Σfx ÷ Σf.

questions.q: For grouped data 0-10 (freq 3) and 10-20 (freq 2), the estimated mean uses which x-values?
questions.explain: For grouped data we use the midpoint of each class as the representative value: 5 and 15.

questions.q: Groups: 0-10 (freq 3, mid 5), 10-20 (freq 2, mid 15). Estimate the mean.
Which sampling method gives every member of the population an equal chance of selection?
questions.explain: In a simple random sample every member has an equal, independent chance of being chosen.

questions.q: A sample is described as 'biased'. What does this mean?
options: It is not representative of the population
questions.explain: A biased sample systematically over- or under-represents part of the population, so it is not representative.

questions.q: In a pie chart, how many degrees represent the whole data set?
questions.explain: A full pie chart is a complete circle, representing 360°.

questions.q: In a pie chart of 40 people, 10 chose football. What angle represents football?
In a histogram, what is plotted on the vertical axis?
questions.explain: Histograms with unequal class widths use frequency density = frequency ÷ class width on the vertical axis.

questions.q: A class of width 5 has frequency 20. Find its frequency density.
questions.explain: Frequency density = frequency ÷ class width = 20 ÷ 5 = 4.

questions.q: A box plot shows Q1 = 12 and Q3 = 20. Find the interquartile range.
From a cumulative frequency graph, the median of n values is read at which position?
questions.explain: The median corresponds to the middle of the data, read at the cumulative frequency n/2.

questions.q: As one variable increases the other decreases. What type of correlation is this?
questions.explain: When one variable rises as the other falls, the correlation is negative.

questions.q: What is a line of best fit used for on a scatter graph?
options: To estimate values and show the trend
questions.explain: A line of best fit shows the overall trend and allows estimation of one variable from another.

questions.q: Estimating a value outside the range of the plotted data is called what, and why is it unreliable?
options: Extrapolation - the trend may not continue
questions.explain: Reading beyond the data range is extrapolation; the trend seen in the data may not hold outside it, so it is unreliable.

questions.q: Two data sets have the same mean but set A has a larger range. What does this tell you?
options: Set A has a higher average
Set A is more spread out (less consistent)
questions.explain: A larger range means greater spread, so set A is less consistent even though the averages match.

questions.q: When comparing two distributions, a good answer refers to which two things?
options: An average and a measure of spread
questions.explain: Comparisons should mention an average (e.g. median or mean) AND a measure of spread (e.g. range or IQR).
